rules.headline: Abacavir is not recommended in HLA-B*57:01-positive patients
rules.rationale: CPIC does not recommend abacavir for individuals with the HLA-B*57:01 allele and advises it only under exceptional circumstances; DPWG advises avoiding it; the French RNPGx guidance calls it contraindicated.
rules.mechanism: Immune-mediated hypersensitivity reaction associated with HLA-B*57:01.

rules.headline: Avoid allopurinol in HLA-B*58:01-positive patients
rules.rationale: CPIC recommends avoiding allopurinol in HLA-B*58:01 carriers because of markedly increased risk of severe cutaneous adverse reactions; DPWG advises an alternative drug or induction of allopurinol tolerance.
rules.mechanism: HLA-B*58:01 is associated with severe cutaneous adverse reactions (SJS/TEN, DRESS).
limitations: DPWG offers 'induction of tolerance' as an alternative to avoidance; that approach is not encoded here.

alternatives.text: No specific alternative is encoded; see the cited guidelines.

rules.mechanism: HLA-B*15:02 is associated with SJS/TEN with carbamazepine.

rules.rationale: CPIC recommends alternative non-tramadol analgesics for ultrarapid metabolizers because of potential life-threatening toxicity from higher morphine exposure; CPNDS advises avoiding codeine for pain relief.

limitations: CPIC and DPWG differ for intermediate metabolizers (DPWG also allows a doubled dose); no dose is calculated here.

rules.headline: SLCO1B1 decreased function: alternative statin, or limit simvastatin dose
rules.rationale: CPIC recommends an alternative statin chosen by desired potency; if simvastatin is warranted in decreased/possible-decreased function the dose is limited to below 20 mg/day. DPWG differs: for the 521 TC genotype, if no alternative, avoid doses above 40 mg/day. The sources are not in agreement on the limit.
rules.mechanism: SLCO1B1 transports statins into the liver; reduced function raises systemic exposure and myopathy risk.
monitoring: Monitor for muscle symptoms; advise patients to report them.
limitations: CPIC and DPWG dose limits differ (CPIC <20 mg/day; DPWG >40 mg/day to be avoided). No reconciliation is attempted.

rules.headline: Increased tacrolimus starting dose recommended for CYP3A5 expressors (normal/intermediate metabolizers)
rules.rationale: CPIC recommends increasing the starting dose by 1.5 to 2 times the recommended starting dose for CYP3A5 expressors (CYP3A5*1 carriers); DPWG and RNPGx make the same recommendation. Dose must be individualised by TDM.
rules.mechanism: CYP3A5 (*1 allele) metabolises tacrolimus extensively in the gut and liver; expressors have lower tacrolimus exposure at standard doses.
monitoring: Therapeutic drug monitoring (TDM) is mandatory for tacrolimus; adjust dose to target trough concentrations per transplant protocol.
limitations: The fold-increase depends on transplant organ and protocol. No dose is calculated here. Liver transplant recipients require special consideration (donor CYP3A5 genotype matters for hepatic clearance).

rules.mechanism: CYP2C9 metabolises (S)-warfarin; reduced activity raises warfarin exposure, increasing bleeding risk.

rules.mechanism: VKORC1 encodes the warfarin target; the -1639A allele reduces VKORC1 expression, making patients more sensitive to warfarin.
monitoring: Frequent INR monitoring. Adjust dose to target INR using a pharmacogenomics-guided algorithm.

rules.headline: Warfarin dose may need adjustment for CYP4F2 variant carriers
rules.rationale: CPIC includes CYP4F2 rs2108622 in its warfarin dosing algorithm; the *3 variant reduces vitamin K recycling, potentially requiring a slightly higher dose. This modifies the direction of expected dose adjustment compared with CYP2C9/VKORC1.
rules.mechanism: CYP4F2 metabolises vitamin K1; reduced CYP4F2 activity raises vitamin K availability, blunting warfarin effect slightly.
monitoring: INR monitoring as for all warfarin patients.
limitations: The CYP4F2 variant effect on dose is modest and direction is opposite to CYP2C9/VKORC1 variants (may need higher dose). The full algorithm requires all gene inputs. No dose is calculated here.

rules.headline: Alternative hormonal therapy recommended for CYP2D6 poor metabolizers taking tamoxifen
rules.rationale: CPIC recommends alternative hormonal therapy (aromatase inhibitor for postmenopausal women, or ovarian suppression plus aromatase inhibitor for premenopausal women) for CYP2D6 poor metabolizers, as reduced endoxifen formation compromises tamoxifen efficacy; DPWG recommends considering an alternative medication.
rules.mechanism: CYP2D6 converts tamoxifen to endoxifen (the active metabolite); poor metabolizers have markedly reduced endoxifen levels and reduced anti-oestrogenic effect.
monitoring: Consider endoxifen plasma level monitoring if tamoxifen is continued despite poor metabolizer status.
limitations: The evidence base is for breast cancer prevention/treatment; applicability to other indications is not established. CPIC recommendation is for postmenopausal vs premenopausal women; sex/menopausal status is not collected.

alternatives.text: Aromatase inhibitor (postmenopausal) or ovarian suppression + aromatase inhibitor (premenopausal) per CPIC.

rules.headline: Irinotecan dose reduction recommended for UGT1A1 poor metabolizers (*28/*28)
rules.rationale: DPWG recommends dose reductions for irinotecan starting at 70% of the standard starting dose for UGT1A1 *28/*28 homozygotes (poor metabolizers), with increases guided by neutrophil count; RNPGx and AIOM guidelines make similar recommendations.
rules.mechanism: UGT1A1 glucuronidates the active irinotecan metabolite SN-38; reduced UGT1A1 activity (*28/*28) elevates SN-38 exposure, increasing the risk of severe diarrhoea and neutropenia.
monitoring: Neutrophil count monitoring after each cycle. Dose escalation only if toxicity is acceptable.
